title: Nobody Wants to Read Your Sh*t

questions.q: What must every piece of writing have before you start, per Pressfield?
a: A concept that gives a fresh angle
A long list of research sources
A strict word count target
A publisher's approval
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to come up with a concept, a unique spin, before writing the first line.

questions.q: What single question can replace the two that cause writer's block?
a: What's the problem here?
Who will read this?
How long should this be?
What does the client want?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says replacing the usual questions with what the problem is removes much resistance.

questions.q: Why do underdog brands like 7Up and Avis succeed, per the summary?
a: They turn their second-place status into an angle
They spend more on advertising than rivals
They copy the market leader closely
They lower prices below everyone else
questions.why: Lesson 1 says number two players can turn silver into gold by embracing their underdog position.

a: A beginning, a middle and an end
A hook, a list and a summary
An intro, a quote and a call to action
A problem, a solution and a bonus
questions.why: Lesson 3 says all great storytellers use beginning, middle and end, however the parts are labeled.

questions.q: What does the first act of a story need to do?
a: Make the reader curious about what happens next
Introduce every character in detail
Resolve the main conflict
Summarize the ending
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the first part kicks off the story and makes us curious about what will happen.
